summary: A 110-ft CCC-built steel tower from 1936 in the Hoosier National Forest, staffed about 40 years until the late 1970s, restored in 1989, and now the last of eight original towers in the forest.

facts.design: 110-ft steel Aermotor tower with 7x7 ft cab; originally 123 wooden steps, now 133 steel steps
facts.status_note: Restored in 1989; no longer staffed since the late 1970s

access.note: No source consulted states current public access or climbability; it sits within the Charles C. Deam Wilderness on the Hoosier National Forest

events.note: Manning ceased in the late 1970s as other fire-detection technology replaced it (approximate; Wikipedia says 'late 1970s')
Tower was restored in 1989 per NHLR; wooden steps replaced with steel ones
Added to National Historic Lookout Register in October 1990, first Indiana tower so listed

evidence.supports: location on edge of Deam Wilderness, Hoosier NF
evidence.quote: Hickory Ridge Lookout is located on the edge of the Charles C. Deam Wilderness on the Hoosier National Forest in Indiana.

evidence.supports: 110-ft steel tower, 7x7 cab, built by CCC 1936, last remaining of eight
evidence.quote: It is a 110-foot steel tower with 7- by 7-ft. cab built by the CCC in 1936 and is the last remaining fire tower, out of an original number of eight, remaining on National Forest land in Indiana.
Construction of the tower began in 1936 under the auspices of the Civilian Conservation Corps.

evidence.supports: steel tower, 7-ft square cab, alidade device
evidence.quote: It is constructed of steel with a seven-foot square 'cab' on the top where the lookout was posted with various equipment including an alidade device used to help locate the location of fire outbreaks.

evidence.supports: 123 wooden steps originally, now 133 steel steps
evidence.quote: As constructed, the tower included 123 wooden steps to provide access to the cab Following a refurbishment of the tower, the wooden steps were replaced. Today, there are 133 steel steps.

evidence.supports: cabin, latrine, garage once on site, now only tower remains
evidence.quote: Originally there was a cabin or guard station, a latrine, and a garage built on the site. All but the tower have now been removed.

evidence.supports: staffed ~40 years during high fire danger, crew at base
evidence.quote: The tower was staffed during periods of high fire danger for approximately 40 years. During such times, a small team of fire fighters was stationed at the base of the tower to respond to fire reports as needed.

evidence.supports: up to 4-5 fires a day at peak, largest came within half a mile
evidence.quote: Some peak times saw as many as four to five fires per day. One of these fires, one of the largest on record for the area, came within half a mile (800 meters) of the tower before it was stopped.

evidence.supports: tower never burned, struck by lightning
evidence.quote: The tower never endured a fire, though it has been struck by lightning.

evidence.supports: manning ceased late 1970s, replaced by other technology; last of eight towers
evidence.quote: Manning of the tower ceased in the late 1970s as the need for the tower had been replaced by other technologies. The tower was one of eight located in the Hoosier National Forest, but is now the only tower remaining.

evidence.supports: added to NHLR October 1990, first Indiana tower listed
evidence.quote: It was added to the National Historic Lookout Register in October 1990, the first such tower in Indiana to be listed.

evidence.supports: no NHLR sign posted, not currently staffed, no volunteer program noted
